dimension.category_description: How users, artifacts, examples, parameters, or user-state signals specify intent and shape the system's next behavior.
dimension.classification_boundary: Requires a user-facing specification or adaptive interaction; invisible sensing infrastructure is excluded.

candidates.title: StepWrite: Adaptive Planning for Speech-Driven Text Generation
candidates.why: StepWrite uses an adaptive Q&A dialogue to incrementally populate task-relevant context and then synthesizes that accumulated specification into a coherent draft. It is a particularly consequential instance because question-driven elicitation replaces conventional prompt composition in a hands-free, eyes-free writing workflow.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over Socrates because the elicited answers specify a complete writing output under a meaningful accessibility constraint, making the inversion both more comprehensive and more consequential.
candidates.pattern_summary: The system takes the interrogative turn: it poses questions — clarification prompts, structured fields, interview turns — and the user's answers, rather than a user-composed prompt, constitute the specification the system works from.
candidates.structural_signature: A system-authored question precedes any user content at the head of the loop, and each reply is written into the input record consumed by the next stage. The set of questions determines which slots of the specification exist, so the user never composes a full specification unprompted.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final three follow the consensus top three; no score required an adjustment. I retained StepWrite and Socrates above the email example for their broader adaptive mechanisms and higher consequential impact, while recognizing that the email example has the clearest literal structural evidence. Readers should distrust any strong claim that StepWrite or Socrates necessarily asks the very first question before all user content: their excerpts establish adaptive questioning and downstream use, but do not expose the complete turn sequence or input-record schema. The email excerpt clearly establishes system-generated questions and user answers, but only implies rather than explicitly describes how those answers are assembled into the final reply. GenerativeGUI was excluded despite unusually concrete JSON evidence because the excerpt suggests clarification inside an already-started chat, conflicting with the strict head-of-loop signature.

candidates.title: Socrates: Data Story Generation via Adaptive Machine-Guided Elicitation of User Feedback
candidates.why: Socrates makes the elicitation policy part of generation: the machine adaptively selects questions, records the user's feedback, and incorporates it into the resulting data story. This clearly demonstrates how system-authored questions can progressively determine a generative specification.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over the email-reply system because its adaptive question selection demonstrates a more general mixed-initiative mechanism than eliciting answers from one fixed source artifact.

candidates.why: The system derives short questions from an incoming email, and the user's answers constitute the specification for a reply instead of requiring the user to compose either a full response or a generative prompt. candidates.title: AI-Instruments: Embodying Prompts as Instruments to Abstract & Reflect Graphical Interface Commands as General-Purpose Tools
candidates.why: The system decomposes an existing image into image-specific prompt fragments, renders those dimensions as individually editable controls, and regenerates the image when a fragment changes. The evidence directly captures the complete derivation–control–downstream-operation chain and makes the content-dependent nature of the controls unusually easy to reconstruct.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above GazeNoter because its evidence explicitly shows both artifact-specific derivation and regeneration after editing, while GazeNoter’s quotation is truncated before fully documenting the downstream effect.
candidates.pattern_summary: The system derives a set of discrete terms, attributes, or dimensions from the material at hand and then puts that derived set on screen as the thing the user manipulates.
candidates.structural_signature: A derivation step produces a finite list of named items from the current input; those items are rendered as individually addressable widgets (chips, rows, sliders, editable fields); manipulating them re-parameterizes the downstream operation. The handle set is regenerated when the input changes, so the control panel's contents are data-dependent rather than fixed at design time.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus order by selecting rank 4, DesignWeaver, instead of rank 3, Composable Prompting Workspaces. DesignWeaver more clearly satisfies the defining derivation step: its controls come from generated images, whereas the evidence for Composable Prompting Workspaces establishes dynamic widgets and downstream influence but not artifact-specific extraction or regeneration when the artifact changes. I raised DesignWeaver from 4.27 to 4.40; no adjustment exceeds 0.3. Evidence caveats: GazeNoter’s quotation is truncated, and DesignWeaver’s abstract leaves the exact control-to-regeneration loop and handle regeneration behavior implicit. Even AI-Instruments’ otherwise strong figure evidence does not explicitly state whether its fragment set is automatically regenerated after every input change.

candidates.why: GazeNoter extracts context keywords from the user’s latest spoken sentence, exposes those input-dependent terms for selection, and uses the selections to shape candidate sentences. It is a strong example of replacing repeated free-text specification with a dynamically derived set of discrete handles.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above DesignWeaver because the evidence explicitly ties keyword derivation to the latest input and selection to candidate text, whereas DesignWeaver’s regeneration response is only implicit.

candidates.title: Codesigning Ripplet: an LLM-Assisted Assessment Authoring System Grounded in a Conceptual Model of Teachers' Workflows
candidates.why: A manual edit to one finished question is interpreted, generalized into a reusable edit command, and applied to other questions—the clearest complete demonstration-to-operative-specification loop in the candidates.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Selected over GenNI because the evidence explicitly shows the demonstration, induction rationale, materialized reusable structure, and subsequent reuse, whereas GenNI's quote does not explicitly show later application.
candidates.pattern_summary: Instead of describing what they want, the user supplies one or more instances of it, and the system generalizes or inverts those instances into the operative specification.
candidates.structural_signature: The input slot accepts finished exemplars; an induction step converts them into a reusable structure (template, constraint set, parameter assignment, recorded macro); that structure, and not the exemplars, is what conditions later runs and what the user can edit. Adding or removing exemplars changes the induced structure.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained the consensus top three and their order after checking the structural signature. I slightly lowered AI-Instruments because its abstract-level quote does not expose the grounding interaction, later execution, or user editability; that third selection is consequently less secure than the first two. GenNI also lacks explicit evidence of later reuse or editing of the inferred control states. Ripplet has the strongest evidence, although the supplied quote still does not explicitly say whether users can inspect or revise the inferred command. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3.

candidates.title: GANSpiration: Balancing Targeted and Serendipitous Inspiration in User Interface Design with Style-Based Generative Adversarial Network
candidates.why: GANSpiration is the cleanest structural match: it ingests the user’s preliminary design image, encodes that artifact into latent conditioning state, and uses it to generate design inspiration whose output changes with the supplied draft.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above CareerCraft because the evidence establishes an unambiguous artifact-to-conditioning-state path, without relying partly on text that may have been authored specifically for the interaction.
candidates.pattern_summary: An artifact the user already possesses or has produced — a draft, a collection, a document, a physical or staged arrangement, their own prior judgments — is ingested and used as the input the generation is conditioned on.
candidates.structural_signature: The system exposes an ingestion path for a user-owned artifact (upload, parse, encode, capture) and routes it into the generator as conditioning state, either directly or after an encoding step. The generation cannot run without that artifact; changing it changes the output. The material is pre-existing with respect to the interaction — it is not authored in order to specify the request.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I promoted GANSpiration from third to first because its quote most completely exposes the structural signature: artifact ingestion, latent encoding, and downstream transformation. I retained CareerCraft but placed it second because its uploaded-document path is strong while its free-text reflections may have been produced for the workflow. I selected the immersive-memory system over consensus runner-up TubeLens: TubeLens is conceptually compelling, but its high rater spread and missing import/consent and inference details make it weaker as a reconstructable structural exemplar. Readers should also distrust any implication that the available quotes fully document the interfaces: GANSpiration’s quote omits the later generation controls, CareerCraft does not distinguish pre-existing from workflow-authored reflections, and the immersive-memory quote does not specify its capture or upload interaction.

candidates.title: TaleBrush: Visual Sketching of Story Generation with Pretrained Language Models
candidates.why: TaleBrush makes surprise a persistent, ordered generation property that writers specify spatially by drawing a level trajectory, providing an unusually clear and expressive realization of the pattern.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over the personalization slider because its drawable trajectory demonstrates that the pattern can control a property across an artifact, not merely set one global scalar.
candidates.pattern_summary: A property of the system or of its output is bound to an ordered control the user sets to a value — a slider, a numbered keypress, a discrete set of levels, a spatial distance.
candidates.structural_signature: A named parameter with an ordered range (short/moderate/long; 1D distance; temperature; abstraction level) is surfaced as a persistent control widget bound to that range. The control does not create content; it scales an already-defined property of whatever content is produced, and the same control is available for every output. Multiple such parameters may be exposed together as a configuration panel.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by promoting rid 15614 from fourth to second and excluding third-ranked rid 5199. CoBRA’s quote proves that users specify a bias value on a 0–4 scale, but it does not show that the value is surfaced as a persistent control widget or that changing it re-runs generation; it therefore demonstrates the subject matter more clearly than the full structure. ImaginationVellum remains selected for design-space coverage, but its evidence is compressed and does not explicitly describe the interaction-and-rerender sequence. TaleBrush’s figure evidence similarly does not state regeneration verbatim, while rid 15614 has the strongest end-to-end evidence. No selected score was adjusted by more than 0.3 from its consensus mean.

candidates.title: Leveraging ChatGPT for Adaptive Learning through Personalized Prompt-based Instruction: A CS1 Education Case Study
candidates.why: This is the strongest structural exemplar: topics and subtopics form the content units, while every unit is supported by the same four named prompt actions—Explanation, Example, Exercise, and Exercise Solution—producing a clear units × actions interaction space.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Jamplate because the evidence explicitly associates one complete, repeated four-action vocabulary with both topics and subtopics, whereas Jamplate does not establish that all three questions appear for every unit.
candidates.pattern_summary: Instead of an open input box, the system attaches the same small, named menu of prepared prompts to every content unit it holds.
candidates.structural_signature: The content is partitioned into units; a fixed vocabulary of n named actions is defined once, system-wide; each unit exposes all n as invocable affordances, and invocation binds (action, unit) into a generation call. The action set does not vary by unit and is not editable by the user, so the interaction space is exactly units × actions. Transplants to any repository of units — a codebase with a fixed per-function action menu, a document set with a fixed per-section menu.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final selection retains the consensus top three; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The main evidentiary weakness is that none of the excerpts explicitly proves every requirement of the strict signature: system-wide invariance, non-editability, and universal availability on every unit. This uncertainty is smallest for rid 7932. Jamplate does not conclusively show that every competitor or column receives all three questions, and LADICA neither names the relation-type vocabulary nor explicitly confirms that it is identical across all notes. These are therefore structural exemplars based on the supplied interface descriptions, not definitive proof of exact Cartesian completeness.

candidates.title: CanvasPic: An Interactive Tool for Freely Generating Facial Images Based on Spatial Layout
candidates.why: CanvasPic is the canonical Spatial Canvas exemplar: users reposition images on a two-dimensional layout, and the distances between them continuously determine each image attribute’s influence on the generated face. Moving unchanged elements therefore changes the request and its output through an explicit, inspectable spatial mapping.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It outranks Component-Wise Sketching because multiple pairwise distances continuously shape generation, making the whole spatial arrangement a richer specification than selection by distance to a single fixed center.
candidates.pattern_summary: The user places elements on an open two-dimensional surface and the system reads their positions and relations as specification.
candidates.structural_signature: Elements are freely positionable on an unbounded surface; the system's input is derived from the configuration — coordinates, distances, containment, or explicit links — and not only from the elements' contents. candidates.title: ImaginationVellum: Generative-AI Ideation Canvas with Spatial Prompts, Generative Strokes, and Ideation History
candidates.why: Generative Strokes are an especially exact match: both the geometry and placement of freehand marks directly modulate generation and latent semantic or stylistic parameters on an ideation canvas.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over Reframer because the evidence explicitly establishes stroke geometry and spatial placement as generative controls, rather than referring more generally to the canvas state as conditioning.
candidates.pattern_summary: The user's freehand mark — a stroke, a scribble, an arrow, a drawn layout — is taken as input to generation, either alongside or in place of a written prompt.
candidates.structural_signature: A drawing surface captures freehand vector input; the captured strokes are passed to the generator as conditioning signal; the generated result is returned into or beside the same surface so it can be drawn on again. The stroke's shape and placement are consumed as content, so two different strokes in the same location yield different results.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by promoting ImaginationVellum from third to first and Reframer from fifth to second because their supplied evidence most directly establishes the structural signature: freehand geometry becomes conditioning state on a canvas that also holds the generated result. I retained Code Shaping but reduced its 4.90 consensus by 0.35 because the evidence does not spell out the annotation vocabulary or precisely show how edited output is returned for another drawing pass. I excluded consensus runner-up Notational Animating: it clearly maps placed motion marks to generated keyframes, but the quote does not establish the required return-and-redraw loop. Readers should also treat ImaginationVellum’s iteration loop and Reframer’s repeated drawing passes as only implicit in the supplied excerpts.

candidates.title: Interactive Table Synthesis With Natural Language
candidates.why: Natural language is explicitly the primary interaction modality for transforming a separate table artifact, making substitution for a complex transformation-control vocabulary the system’s central claim.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It edges out Stylette because “primary interaction modality” provides stronger evidence that language substitutes for conventional controls, while table transformations also demonstrate a broader operational repertoire than styling alone.
candidates.pattern_summary: The user states in language what they want to be true of the artifact, and the system performs the corresponding edit or retrieval.
candidates.structural_signature: The artifact has an established non-linguistic control vocabulary (transformation functions, palette editors, query forms, element handles). The interface exposes a text or utterance field as the operative control over that artifact, parses the utterance into the operation, and applies it; the user names an outcome rather than a procedure. The artifact itself remains a separate object from the language channel — the utterance is about it, not an entry in it.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by excluding rid 350 and rid 3216 and promoting rid 11389. AVA is conceptually compelling, but its supplied quote says only “user instructions,” not natural language, so the evidence does not establish the pattern’s defining channel. LLMR explicitly names natural language, but its quote does not show that users state outcomes rather than procedures; NL2Color does. Readers should distrust any strong claim that these systems eliminate parallel direct-manipulation controls: none of the supplied excerpts proves that conventional handles are unavailable, although rid 11792’s “primary interaction modality” comes closest. No selected score was adjusted by more than 0.3.

candidates.title: AI Kitchen: Child-Readable Ingredient Labels and Transparency Stickers for Failure Anticipation and Reliance Calibration
candidates.why: AI Kitchen adopts a coherent kitchen vocabulary—ingredient cards, recipes, testing, traps, and product stickers—and maps its familiar actions directly onto training-data selection, model testing, reliance practice, and transparency export.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above FusAIn because the evidence identifies several source-domain objects and actions alongside their corresponding AI operations, demonstrating the full structural signature rather than one especially clean mapping.
candidates.pattern_summary: The system borrows the vocabulary of an already-known artifact — a spreadsheet, a paint palette, a plant, a social feed — and uses it wholesale as the surface through which the user acts, rather than devising controls specific to the underlying operation.
candidates.structural_signature: The interface presents the objects of a source domain external to the system and accepts that domain's operations as its input actions; each such action is translated into a system operation, so the two sets stand in one-to-one correspondence. What is on screen is the source domain's objects and their legal actions, whether or not the paper states the mapping.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by placing AI Kitchen first and FusAIn second, ahead of PromptPaint. The adjustment reflects structural evidence: AI Kitchen enumerates multiple metaphor-to-system correspondences, while FusAIn gives the clearest single action-to-operation mapping. PromptPaint remains selected because the borrowed painting interaction is explicitly the steering mechanism, but its score is reduced because the evidence names media such as oil and watercolor without specifying individual gestures or their system effects. No score differs from the consensus by more than 0.3. Readers should treat all three mappings as supported by very short abstract/figure excerpts rather than complete interaction descriptions; AI Kitchen’s quote is broad but does not prove every kitchen term has a strict one-to-one system correspondence, and PromptPaint is especially underspecified at that level.
